cohort: Pregnant women from 7 sites in low-resource settings (Kenya, Zambia, India, Pakistan, Guatemala, and Argentina)
finding: Stillbirth rates were high but decreased in most sites during the study period, and several factors were associated with increased risk of stillbirth, including being less educated, older, having less access to antenatal care, and not being delivered by a skilled birth attendant.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were 7.6% among women with stillbirths, with obstructed labor being the primary indication (36.9%).
country: Kenya, Zambia, India, Pakistan, Guatemala, Argentina
gest_age: Preterm birth was associated with increased risk of stillbirth
